explain.narrative:
## Project: Student Grade Manager

Keep score validation separate from grade calculation, and define whether grade boundaries are inclusive. A collection can hold records, while methods make each operation testable.

## Applying the concept

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that directly supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failure cases and state assumptions clearly.

## Verification checklist

- Compile with JDK 21.
- Predict the output before running.
- Test normal, boundary and invalid inputs where relevant.
- Check resource cleanup and error handling.
- Prefer explicit types and focused methods.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int[] scores = {80, 90, 100}; int total = 0; for (int score : scores) total += score; System.out.println(total / scores.length); } }

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int score = 85; String grade = score >= 90 ? "A" : score >= 80 ? "B" : score >= 70 ? "C" : "D"; System.out.println(grade); } }
examples.explanation: Maps a validated score to a grade band.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int score = 105; System.out.println(score >= 0 && score <= 100 ? "valid" : "invalid"); } }
examples.explanation: Rejects a score outside the permitted range.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { record Student(String name, int score) {} Student s = new Student("Mira", 92); System.out.println(s.name() + ": " + s.score()); } }
examples.explanation: Uses a record to represent a student result.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int[] scores = {65, 72, 88}; int passed = 0; for (int s : scores) if (s >= 70) passed++; System.out.println("passed=" + passed); } }
examples.explanation: Produces a summary count using a clear passing threshold.
